bad.title: Nine fields, all shouting
bad.text: Every label is bold caps and every value 17px bold, so people read all nine to find one.
bad.wait: Press Glance, then pick a gate, to see this.

bad.title: Gate B21 hides in the middle
bad.text: It’s red, but so are Flight and Boarding. In one second, most people miss it.
bad.wait: Press Glance, then pick a gate, to see this.

good.title: Gate and Boarding at 30px
good.text: The two things people check at the airport sit on top, set off by a dashed line.
good.wait: Press Glance, then pick a gate, to see this.

good.title: The other seven step down
good.text: Small gray labels and smaller values stay readable, but don’t compete for the glance.
good.wait: Press Glance, then pick a gate, to see this.

bad.title: Push looks like a setting row
bad.text: Same 14px and weight as Messages below it. Only a blue tint sets it apart.

bad.title: In gray, the sections run together
bad.text: Nine lines of the same text. People can’t see where Email ends and Push begins.
bad.wait: Turn on Grayscale to see this.

good.title: Push is bigger, bolder, set apart
good.text: 16px bold with space above it starts a new group at a glance.

good.title: Still clear without the blue
good.text: Size, weight and space carry the order, so the color is only extra.
good.wait: Turn on Grayscale to see this.

bad.title: Serves 4 and 25 minutes don’t match
bad.text: Two facts of the same kind in two sizes and two weights. Which one matters more?

bad.title: Eight styles for one card
bad.text: From 22px down to 12px, mostly 1 to 3px apart. Too close to read as an order.
bad.wait: Turn on Show styles to see this.

good.title: Serves 4 · 25 minutes on one line
good.text: Both key facts share one style, so they read as one level.

good.title: Four styles, each a clear step
good.text: Title, key facts, body, small print. Ingredients reuses the key-fact style instead of adding one.
good.wait: Turn on Show styles to see this.

bad.title: Continue shopping looks like the way on
bad.text: Filled and first in line, so some people press it and land back in the shop.

bad.title: Check out gets no extra weight
bad.text: Same fill, same size. People have to read both to find the next step.

good.title: Continue shopping steps back
good.text: Still there for people who want it, but outlined, so it doesn’t compete.

good.title: Check out is the only fill
good.text: The eye lands there first, and that’s the step after the bag.

bad.title: Lake, June floats between photos
bad.text: 12px above and 12px below, so it could label photo 2 or photo 3.

bad.title: Photo 3 seems to own the caption
bad.text: Many people read captions as headings for what follows, and pick this one.

good.title: Lake, June hugs its photo
good.text: 4px under photo 2 and 20px before photo 3. The gap says where it belongs.

good.title: Photo 3 starts a new group
good.text: The wider gap above it shows that Lake, June isn’t its label.

bad.title: A box around every single row
bad.text: Name, Email and Phone each get a frame, inside the frame of their group.

bad.title: A rule plus two box edges
bad.text: Three lines mark one break between Profile and Privacy.

bad.title: 10 lines for five settings
bad.text: People read past more lines than words, and the page looks busy.
bad.wait: Turn on Show lines to see this.

good.title: Rows sit on plain space
good.text: No frames needed. Name, Email and Phone still read as one group.

good.title: A 20px gap instead of a rule
good.text: The bigger gap and the Privacy label do what the lines and boxes did.

bad.title: The slider moves, the photo doesn’t
bad.text: Dragging Brightness changes nothing yet, so people think it’s broken.

bad.title: Apply sits past four other options
bad.text: It’s below Crop, Rotate, Filter and Frame, out of sight until people scroll.

good.title: Slider and button as a pair
good.text: The button sits right under the slider, so people see they work together.

good.title: Apply is in view from the start
good.text: No scrolling past Crop, Rotate, Filter and Frame to find it.

bad.title: The error hugs Postcode
bad.text: 22px under Phone and 3px above Postcode, so people check the postcode first.
bad.wait: Press Create account to see this.

bad.title: The real problem sits far above
bad.text: The a at the end of the phone number is what needs fixing.

good.title: Tight under Phone
good.text: 5px under the field and 20px before Postcode. It reads as part of Phone.
good.wait: Press Create account to see this.

good.title: The field it’s about, right above
good.text: People look up from the message and spot the a at the end of 12a.

bad.title: Three rows, two different gaps
bad.text: 7px above Lemons and 11px below. People see a wobble, not a choice.

bad.title: 19 above the button, 15 below
bad.text: Close to 16, but not quite, so the card looks slightly off.

bad.title: Seven sizes for one card
bad.text: From 3 to 19px, none of them repeating on purpose.
bad.wait: Turn on Show gaps to see this.

good.title: 8px above and below every row
good.text: The ingredients sit evenly, so they read as one list.

good.title: 24 before the button, 16 after
good.text: A full step more than the rows, so the action stands apart on purpose.

good.title: Four steps, each one used again
good.text: 4, 8, 16 and 24. Every gap has a reason a review can name.
good.wait: Turn on Show gaps to see this.

bad.title: The dates sit 2px to the right
bad.text: Too small to mean anything, but big enough to look like a slip.

bad.title: Total pokes out to the left
bad.text: The price row and its rule start 3px before the title.

bad.title: The note is off by 4px
bad.text: Free cancellation is pushed in a little. It reads as a mistake, not a note.

good.title: The dates share the title’s edge
good.text: Every line starts at 16px, so the card reads as one clean column.

good.title: Total lines up too
good.text: The price row and its rule start on the same edge as the rest.

good.title: Indented by a full step
good.text: 32px in, with a green bar. Free cancellation reads as a note on the price.

bad.title: Playlist rows are cramped
bad.text: Tiny thumbnails, no song count and a small tap target. Easy to hit the wrong one.

bad.title: Recently played is roomy
bad.text: Rows nearly three times as tall. Scrolling between lists feels like two apps.

good.title: One row height for both lists
good.text: Every row has a 32px thumbnail and its count, so tapping feels the same everywhere.

good.title: Recently played, same rhythm
good.text: Crossing into the second list changes nothing but the heading.

bad.title: The address fades to pale gray
bad.text: It’s the line people need at the door, and the hardest to read.

bad.title: Order 4821 is fainter still
bad.text: People who need the order number for support have to squint at it.

bad.title: In sunlight, the text is gone
bad.text: The glare washes out the pale gray. Only the heading is left.
bad.wait: Turn on Bright sunlight to see this.

good.title: The address in full text color
good.text: Far above 4.5 : 1, so it holds up on a dim screen or in sun.

good.title: A quieter caption that still passes
good.text: It steps back from the body text without dropping below 4.5 : 1.

good.title: Still readable in the glare
good.text: The same sunlight leaves every line, even the caption, easy to read.
good.wait: Turn on Bright sunlight to see this.

bad.title: €18.50, in or out?
bad.text: Only the green says Ana paid it back. Nothing else on the row does.

bad.title: Without color, five lookalike amounts
bad.text: Salary and Rent read the same, so people can’t tell what came in.
bad.wait: Turn on Remove color to see this.

good.title: +€18.50 with an arrow
good.text: The sign and the arrow say money came in, with or without the green.

good.title: Received, in words
good.text: The word sits under the name, where people already look.

good.title: Still clear in gray
good.text: Signs, arrows and words carry the meaning. Color only speeds up the scan.
good.wait: Turn on Remove color to see this.

bad.title: Taken and free, equally light
bad.text: With red-green color blindness, B3 looks just like the free B2 next to it.

bad.title: The legend can’t help
bad.text: Its chips use the same two colors, so it can’t settle which is which.

good.title: Taken is dark and crossed out
good.text: Even with the colors muddied, B3 is darker and has a cross, so nobody picks it.

good.title: Free is light with a green edge
good.text: Light seats read as open in any color vision.

bad.title: Light-theme gray, reused in dark
bad.text: On the dark card, “Bring your insurance card” sinks into the background.

bad.title: Passes in Light, fails in Dark
bad.text: In Dark the same caption drops to 2.5 : 1, far below 4.5 : 1.

good.title: Its own gray in each theme
good.text: Dark gets a lighter, warmer gray, so the caption stays readable.

good.title: Each theme measured on its own
good.text: Light 6.1 : 1 and Dark 6.2 : 1. Both pairs pass.
